title: 跑步成社交名片：高端装备热销，谁在买单？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: And even though this is an activity that does not require more than shorts, shirts, shoes, running has become a big business. We talked to Lily Meyer about what's become
segments.zh: 尽管跑步只需要短裤、T恤和跑鞋，但它已成为一门大生意。我们采访了莉莉·迈耶，聊聊这项价值数十亿美元的产业。

segments.en: a multi-billion dollar industry. She's a retail reporter for Bloomberg.
segments.zh: 她是彭博社的零售记者。

segments.en: Lily, you're right about how running has become a status symbol. When and how did that happen?
segments.zh: 莉莉，你说得对，跑步已成为一种身份象征。这是何时发生的？又是如何发生的？

segments.en: Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, running has always been popular, but coming out of the pandemic as run clubs regathered and began more people joined and got into running.
segments.zh: 是的，跑步一直很受欢迎，但疫情后，跑步俱乐部重新聚集，更多人加入并爱上跑步。

segments.en: Who in the oil who works at Bloomberg Intelligence told you that running has become kind of cultic? Describe that. I mean, I live in Brooklyn near the park. There are running clubs.
segments.zh: 彭博智库的同事告诉我，跑步已变得有点“邪教”意味。我住在布鲁克林公园附近，那里有很多跑步俱乐部。

segments.en: I see groups, but it's more than that. It's become like a real way of life for a lot of people.
segments.zh: 我看到成群结队的人，但不止于此，它已成为很多人的一种生活方式。

segments.en: Yeah, I mean, the running club culture has exploded. There are now running clubs around everything, you know, around different interests. And then there are dating apps where you can meet people
segments.zh: 是的，跑步俱乐部文化爆发了。现在有围绕各种兴趣的跑步俱乐部，还有通过健身认识人的交友应用。

segments.en: through fitness. And so I think it's really become more of an identifier than it was in the past.
segments.zh: 所以我认为，它确实比以前更像一种身份标识。

segments.en: So it's become this kind of cult. How does that play out in terms of the way that people dress for it, what clothes they're buying for, what ancillary gear they're getting as a result
segments.zh: 所以它成了一种“邪教”。这如何体现在人们的穿着、购买的服装以及作为跑者所购买的辅助装备上？

segments.en: of being runners, I guess, in a bigger sense? Yeah, I mean, I think because it's become more social, people want to look good while they do it, if they're going to a run club that has
segments.zh: 是的，因为跑步变得更社交化，人们希望在跑步时看起来不错，如果去参加跑步俱乐部，他们就会想穿得好看。

segments.en: a bar meetup after. And then maybe they see someone they're interested in, they want to look good if they're doing what they're friends or want to make new friends. So I think
segments.zh: 之后还有酒吧聚会。如果他们看到感兴趣的人，想让自己看起来好看，无论是和朋友一起还是想结交新朋友。所以我觉得

segments.en: it's become less of an activity you can do in your pajamas or in your old college t-shirt.
segments.zh: 这已经不再是一件可以穿着睡衣或旧大学T恤就能做的活动了。
